reason: Rate-path signals are genuinely split into a coin-flip the night before FOMC: the CME/Investing.com Fed Rate Monitor (fetched 2026-09-15) prices the September 16 decision at 90.1% hold at 3.75-4.00% and just 9.9% for a cut to 3.50-3.75%, essentially zero hike risk -- while Yahoo Finance's aggregated pre-FOMC headlines the same day report Wall Street increasingly pricing a quarter-point HIKE (Moody's Zandi warning it would be a 'serious mistake'), with the 10-year yield spiking above 5% for the first time since 2023 and chip stocks already selling off on an AI-capex warning. That is exactly the kind of cross-desk disagreement the brief flagged, and it sits on top of a book that is a pure duration-sensitive, no-hedge long small/mid-cap growth book (IWM, SOFI, RKLB, HOOD, XBI) with SOXL already stopped out at 101.13 on 2026-09-14, which itself validated that the downside-protection stops are live and working rather than needing to be re-cut by hand. With ~59% cash already parked (53% plus the freed SOXL weight) as the deliberate downside cushion this book was built around, and every remaining leg carrying a hard stop (-12% to -20%) that will fire mechanically if a surprise hike hits small-cap beta and semis-adjacent names hardest, there is no edge in re-entering fresh legs at unknown pre-FOMC prices only to pay another round of commissions and take on fresh cost basis risk into a binary catalyst landing tomorrow. Better to let the existing stop/cash structure absorb the hike tail while staying positioned for the more probable hold-to-cut outcome that keeps the small-cap growth thesis intact, and reassess with the FOMC statement in hand rather than in front of it.
